title: Compliance for Everyone
subtitle: Eight cards on what compliance really is, before you crack the case, make the calls and play it through.

cards.headline: Rules are not the point. What they protect is.
cards.body: Fourteen people fell ill after a catered lunch. Every rule that could have stopped it was written down. This lesson is about why rules fail and how to make them work.

cards.headline: Compliance is doing what the rules require, and being able to show it
cards.body: Not a department, not a form. A kitchen that keeps chicken at 5 °C and writes the reading down is compliant. One that owns a thermometer is not.

cards.headline: Four places rules come from
points: Standards your organisation signed up to

cards.headline: You meet compliance ten times a day without noticing
cards.body: A parent's data, a tutor's gift, a safety check, a missing record. The quiz puts you in each moment and explains every option, right or wrong.

cards.headline: Why checks exist

number.label: the fridge that looked fine for seventeen days

cards.body: A five-star certificate on the wall, a probe still in its box, and a log filled in on a closed Sunday.

quote.text: An audit is not there to catch you. It is there to find out whether the system works when you are tired.

cards.headline: Culture is what happens when nobody is checking
cards.body: Speaking up, training before the first shift, records that are true. The island tour consolidates all of it and ends with inspection day.

cards.body: Tap any line to jump back to its card.

cards.headline: Start with the case
cards.body: Chapter 1 drops you into the Marigold kitchen with a notebook and twelve clues.
